mail.description: one letter's envelope, sent or received; in an app, read only by its owners and editors, whatever the app's access

name.description: the name it is from, as the reader's mail shows it beside the address

to.description: the address it is written to — absent when `deliver.to` names the recipient as an entity instead

at.description: when it was written, or when it arrived

target.description: the entity this letter is about — any entity at all, so correspondence hangs off the thing it concerns

message_id.description: the Message-ID other mail systems know this letter by — read from a letter that arrived, or returned by the sender for one that left — and what a reply threads on

verified.description: whether the sending domain signed for this letter (DKIM) — false is recorded, never dropped: a letter nobody signed for is still a letter, and the reader is the one who decides what to trust

in_reply_to.description: the Message-ID this letter answers, exactly as the header wrote it — what arrives before `reply_to` can name an entity, and all a reply to a letter nobody kept ever has

reply_address.description: where an answer to this letter goes: for one that arrived, its `Reply-To:` header; for one we send, the `Reply-To:` it leaves with. Absent, an answer goes to `from`

email.description: an address, as an entity — what a person is reachable at

recipient.description: this address is on file only because a letter is for it, and nothing else about it is; in an app, read only by its owners and editors, whatever the app's access — the platform writes it when a letter's `deliver.to` names such an address, as a letter is kept by `mail`

deliver.description: who a letter is for, as an entity in your graph

to.description: the recipient — their address is looked up when the letter goes out

waiting.description: why an outbound letter cannot reach a sender yet; cleared before it is handed over

tried.description: when the letter was handed to the sender — one with this and no outcome may have left, so it is never handed over again

delivered.description: the letter left: half of the outcome pair

channel.description: the delivery channel, when delivery can take more than one route

bounced.description: the letter did not leave: the other half

reason.description: what went wrong, as the sender reported it

refused.description: the provider refused an address on the letter: the address is the writer's to fix, and nothing failed

notified.description: a recipient was told about something

mail_show.title: Read a mail message
mail_show.description: Return one mail message in full: its headers, its body, and one-line summaries of the rest of its thread, with this message marked. The text is returned in content.body alongside the opened mark. Reading marks the caller's subscription to the thread opened, which is why this tool writes where graph_show only reads.

letter.description: the message to read; pass its id or registered name

mail_reply.title: Reply to a mail message
mail_reply.description: Write a reply threaded on one message and request that it be sent. It is addressed to the other side of the original (the sender of a received message, or the recipient of one you sent) from the address the original used, with the subject prefixed `Re:`. Replying to a received message archives the caller's subscription to its thread: a thread you have answered is not waiting on you. The configured sender delivers it; a graph with no sender configured records the reply and never sends it. Returns the applied bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed. Confirm the recipient and message before requesting delivery; a sent email cannot be recalled.

letter.description: the message being replied to; pass its id or registered name

mail_send.title: Send a mail message
mail_send.description: Create a mail message and request that it be sent. It sends from an address this graph holds, through the graph’s own sender, and never from a person’s own mail account: asked to email someone with nothing here named, use whatever mail tool the person has connected. `to` is an email address or the id of an entity in this graph; an address nobody in the graph has becomes a new `email` entity, so the address book grows as mail is sent. `from` defaults to the email address of the entity it is `about`, such as a project’s own, so the answer comes back to that entity; otherwise to the caller’s own email address. Without a configured sender, the message is recorded but not sent. A configured sender delivers it asynchronously and writes `delivered` or `bounced` onto the message. Returns the applied bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed. Confirm the recipient and message before requesting delivery; a sent email cannot be recalled. The initial result is not a delivery receipt; read the message again to check its outcome.

to.description: an email address, or the id of the entity it is for

from.description: the address it is sent from (default: the address of what it is about, else the caller’s own)

about.description: the entity this message is about, so the correspondence is attached to it; pass its id or registered name

mail_check.title: Check the mail
mail_check.description: Check that every received mail message has a sender. Also reports incomplete configuration for a sender this server has configured. A message with a Message-ID but no `from` can never be answered, since a reply has no address to go to. Takes no arguments. Returns a report in content.body, with warning or failure findings when present; it does not repair the records or configuration.

mail_post.description: Hand an outbound letter to the sender and record its outcome. A send the sender knows never left is tried again; an unavailable configured sender defers its recorded run.

mail_task.description: File a letter that arrived for a project, or for an address filed under one, as a task in that project, linked to the letter by an about edge, so it waits on the board until it is answered.

mail_answered.description: Complete the task a letter filed once this graph has delivered a letter answering it: its reply, or one sent about it.

mail_dismissed.description: Archive the letter whose task was cancelled, with the cancel's time and actor: cancelling a letter's task says it needs no answer, so it leaves the unanswered list.

mail.description: one letter's envelope, sent or received; in an app, read only by its owners and editors, whatever the app's access

email.description: an address, as an entity — what a person is reachable at
